name: Whatnot card-display turntable
goal: Slim 12 V worm-gear turntable, 2-5 RPM variable, switchable spin/hold, for a card auction livestream.
requirements: 12 V DC worm-gear motor hidden inside the base; motor output drives a gear on a vertical shaft that carries the plate
Plate speed adjustable, about 2–5 RPM (one turn every 12–30 s)
Rocker switch: spin / hold.  Rotary knob: speed.  Barrel jack for a 12 V wall adapter
Slim: base as low as the motor allows, plate ≥ 200 mm so several cards or a small stand fit
All custom parts 3D-printable on a 220 × 220 × 250 mm bed without supports (plate optionally split in two)
Off-the-shelf parts only from common hobby suppliers; no soldering beyond wires to pads/tabs
Plate removable without tools for shipping; optional card easel that sits on the plate

hardware.part: JGY-370 12 V worm-gear motor, 15 RPM, 6 mm D-shaft
hardware.critical_dims: gearbox 32x37x26, shaft 6 mm D x 14, can dia 24.4

hardware.part: PWM DC motor speed controller 12 V >= 2 A with panel potentiometer

mechanism.train: motor (worm, 15 RPM) -> 17T pinion -> 51T spur gear (3:1) -> rod -> hub -> plate
mechanism.load_path: plate -> hub boss -> top 608 inner race -> lid ledge -> base; bottom 608 locates the rod radially

parts.name: gear
parts.orientation: teeth face down, hub up (selector flips it)

parts.name: hub
parts.orientation: disc face down, hex boss up

steps.done_when: motor, gear train, bearings, PCB and panel parts fit inside base_d with >= 1 mm clearance (CHECK echoes)
centre distance = m*(N1+N2)/2, ratio gives 2-5 RPM with chosen motor
plate weight goes through the bearing inner race, never a printed face
lid screws, panel cutouts, foot recesses present; wall >= min_wall
every part prints flat without supports; inspection passes

applied_lessons.lesson: Sink the lid bearing boss into a recess in the drive gear: it saves ~4 mm of base height versus stacking bearing above gear.
Slimmest vertical-axis stack: fixed post, one bearing inside each rotating part, spacer tube between inner races; height is then set by the pinion OD, not by bearing stacking.
Pocket ceilings printed face-down are flat overhangs the area metric under-reports: give pockets 45 deg conical walls and keep any remaining bridge under ~30 mm.
Orient a gearmotor tangentially (can along the base's circumference) so the base diameter is set by the plate gear, not by motor length.
Right-angle drives for FDM: use a crown (face) gear + spur pinion, not a bevel pair; it prints teeth-up with no overhang and tolerates +-0.5 mm axial pinion position.
Keep >= 2 mm between a rotating disc rim and any static wall; a 0.5 mm graze shows up as <1 mm3 in the interference view but will click when printed.
Build round plates and rims as one rotate_extrude() profile; a union of coincident cylinders leaves a 4-face seam edge and a non-watertight STL.
A part with features on both faces (boss below, hub above) cannot print flat: split the smaller feature into its own part (e.g. a spacer ring) instead of adding supports.
Run an interference view (intersection() of every assembled pair, must be empty) before shipping: a lid locating lip crossing the screw bosses is invisible in renders but shows as ~120 mm3 overlap.
When a pinion meshes a crown/face gear on its centre line, phase the pinion by half a tooth pitch (180/N degrees) or tooth lands on tooth; the interference view catches it.

open_questions: Measure your JGY-370: gearbox height along the shaft (jgy_gb_h) and shaft length set the base height.
